name: LFM3-VL-2B
context_scaling: Native 128,000 from text_config max_position_embeddings (card states 128K input+output); no rope_scaling block. rope_parameters: full_attention uses partial_rotary_factor 0.5 with rope_theta 1,000,000, sliding_attention uses rope_theta 10,000. The vision encoder uses axial RoPE at rope_theta 1,000,000 on 16x16 patches.
attention_variant: Same tri-hybrid LFM3 text stack as LFM3-1.7B: 13 gated short-convolution layers (conv), 5 sliding-window attention layers (sliding_window 256), 6 full-attention layers at indices 2,6,10,14,18,22; GQA 16 heads / 4 KV heads, head_dim 128. Vision encoder is separate: 14 layers = 8 gated depthwise 2D convolutions interleaved with 6 bidirectional full-attention layers, 16x16 patches, spatial_merge_size 2 (each 2x2 patch block becomes one language token).

notes:
ADDED 2026-10-29 from the HF trendingScore feed (rank 6, 1,596 downloads, 145 likes, repo created 2026-10-19). Post-trained vision-language model on LiquidAI/LFM3-1.7B-Base - the same text stack as the catalog's lfm3-1-7b record, plus a new in-house vision encoder.

PARAM DERIVATION: params_b 1.918 = safetensors.total 1,918,181,888 from api/models?blobs=true, and the card breaks it down itself: 1.73B language model + 164M vision encoder + 25M projector. Dense, so active_params_b = params_b = 1.918. flops_per_token_active = 2 x 1.918e9 = 3.836e9, which follows the repo's convention for the vision model (text-only lfm3-1-7b records 3.4576e9 for 1.729B) - it does NOT include the encoder forward per image, which is a prefill-shaped cost per image and not a per-token cost.

KV DERIVATION: kv_cache_bytes_per_token is recorded 0 on the repo's convention for LFM hybrid stacks (no growing per-token cache), matching lfm3-1-7b. The nonzero part, computed from text_config: 6 full_attention layers x 2 (K+V) x 4 KV heads x 128 head_dim x 2 B = 12,288 B/token, PLUS 5 sliding-window layers x 2,048 B/token capped at a 256-token window = 2,621,440 B (2.5 MiB) fixed per sequence, PLUS the 13 conv layers' conv_L_cache 7 state which is constant. So a 128,000-token context costs 128,000 x 12,288 = 1.57 GB of growing KV and then flat. That is the number that matters for this user's box: under 2 GB of cache at full context, on a 1.9B model. The vision encoder adds no KV growth beyond the image tokens it injects, but each image costs tokens: spatial_merge_size 2 over 16x16 patches means one token per 32x32 pixel block, and video is sampled at 2 fps with 4-768 frames by default, which is where a long clip actually blows the budget.

EVIDENCE: the card publishes a real HTML table (73 rows, 62 vision benchmarks) with an explicit LFM3-VL 2B column, a no-think column, and nine competitor columns. It is machine-readable, not a figure - so these rows are transcribed, not read by eye. The card's own claim, verbatim: 'Across 62 vision benchmarks, LFM3-VL-2B scores at least 8 points ahead of all models of similar size. It matches Gemma 4 12B, is within 2 points of GPT-5.6 Luna, and scores higher than Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite.' Its own aggregate average is 71.4 vs Gemma4-12B 71.7 and GPT-5.6 Luna 73.4, so 'matches' is right and 'ahead' is true only against models at or below 4B.

WHY IT EARNS A RECORD: it is a same-test upset over the catalog's own vision-language predecessor lfm2-5-vl-3b (3.1B) despite being 1.9B - BLINK +10.1, ChartQA +12.1, MathVista +15.3, MM-IF Eval +12.2, OCRBench v2 +15.2, ScreenSpot-v2 +13.9, MuirBench +8.2. That is a smaller model beating a larger one from the same vendor on eight of the same named tests, which is the size-class claim the catalog cares about.

LOSES (recorded, not hidden): it beats nothing at 4B or above on knowledge-heavy vision - Qwen3.5-4B wins MMMU 74.6 vs 55.7, MMMU-Pro 67.2 vs 45.7, MathVista 84.8 vs 84.2, MM-IFEval 79.5 vs 72.8, MuirBench 72.8 vs 66.4, OCRBench v2 65.7 vs 63.5; Gemma4-12B wins MMMU 76.7 vs 55.7, MMMU-Pro 69.1 vs 45.7, MME 85.7 vs 86.9 (LOSS for Gemma), MathVista 80.4 vs 84.2 (LOSS for Gemma), CountBenchQA 95.9 vs 93.0. So the picture is consistent: it is the best sub-2B vision model on the card and it loses the hard-knowledge rows to anything at 4B and above. It also loses the tool-use comparison that matters for the catalog: lfm2-5-vl-3b ToolSandBox 59.5 vs this card's MM-ToolSandbox 42.5 (different harnesses, so flagship-vs-flagship is not clean, but the direction is not in its favour). And the card itself says it is 'not recommended for coding, multi-turn conversations, or complex reasoning'.

THINKING-MODE TRAP: this card prints two of its own columns and the gap is enormous - MathVista 84.2 thinking vs 68.5 no-think (15.7 points), We-Math 68.6 vs 20.1 (48.5!), MATH-Vision 51.6 vs 28.4. If the record quoted the no-think column it would look like a much weaker model, and if it quoted thinking without saying so it would overstate default serving. Rows here are the thinking column and each config note says so. This is also why the 8-point-ahead claim is a thinking-mode claim.

HARDWARE GATE: active 1.918B <= 40 and 1.918 x 0.5 GiB = 0.96 GiB <= 128, so it passes easily and is the cheapest thing in this run to actually run - a 4-bit GGUF is about 1.2 GB and the vendor ships GGUF (llama.cpp/LM Studio), MLX 4-bit and ONNX builds from day one, which most records in this catalog cannot say.

GAPS: licence is 'other' (LFM Open License v1.0) - open weights but not OSI, and revenue-gated above a threshold, so it is not a drop-in for a commercial product. No throughput or TTFT numbers are published anywhere on the card, so there is no serving-cost data, only quality rows. 2026-10-29 image triage: every figure on this card was opened and read. 00.png and 01.png are training-pipeline diagrams (pre-training/mid-training token budgets; SFT -> vision RL + mixed RL -> MOPD), not charts. The two unclassified cdn-uploads PNGs are 'LFM3-VL-2B Edge Inference' (prefill tok/s, decode tok/s and memory GB on Ryzen AI Max+ 395 / Apple M5 Max / Galaxy S26 Ultra) and a B300 concurrency-vs-throughput line chart. Both are SPEED measurements, not capability scores, so neither belongs in benchmarks - and the card does not print a serving price or region, so there is nothing to put on a service record either. The edge-chart ordering also does not support the card's prose that this model has the highest prefill on all three devices: it is highest on all three, but MiniCPM-V-4.7-1B beats it on decode throughput on every device (253.5 vs 160.9 on Ryzen, 341.1 vs 286.7 on M5 Max, 60.5 vs 46.7 on S26 Ultra). Recorded here rather than as rows.
